review: did you know that united states of america stole their flag from a mask of character named dallas from 2011 cooperative first-person shooter payday: the heist while another cooperative first-person shooter from valve named left 4 dead stole the idea of payday: the heist and was released in 2006? overkill was robbed, like holy crар.

Payday: The Heist is a first person shooter game developed by Overkill Software and published by Sony Entertainment. The game was released in October 2011 on PC, after being released on PS3. The game is owned on Steam by over four million players due to its regularity being on sale. 

The gameplay is based around completing heists with a party of four people including you. This can be done either in a single player environment, or up to 4 player co-op online. The heists can consist of the classic bank jobs, right the way to the complete extreme of extracting blood from a highly classified patient. You play the role of one of the four main characters in the game, Dallas, Chains, Wolf or Hoxton.  Each member of the team can use a variety of different weapons, you are able to select your load out before jumping into a heist, so once you get to know what is needed to be done on each heist, you can select what to use accordingly. Each of the missions starts off in a stealth style mission, where you have to disable security camera, turning off alarm systems etc. Whether you complete these tasks successfully or not without being seen will determine how the rest of the heist will carry out.  These starting missions are done really well, and you will be fully immersed since most of them have you sneaking around a pitch black building trying to out manoeuvre the guards. A lot of the missions also come with the added obstacle of civilians – these are crucial in any of the heists as you can keep them hostage and use them as bargaining trades should one of your other team mates be captured by the police too. 

Whilst you can spend a good portion of the game in stealth and hopefully not being noticed, a good portion of the game will also be spent with you going all guns blazing as you attempt to fend off an almost endless stream of enemy police and SWAT.  The gunplay in Payday really well done. All of the guns feel as powerful as you would expect, and the choice of weapons is pretty big when compared to other FPS games.  Ammo does become a problem with your primary weapon since you’ll be shooting this off constantly at points, but can be easily countered by the abundance of pickups of ammo off dead enemies. 

Even though Payday is almost four years old at this point, it is still a really good looking game, especially when you ramp up the resolution to 4k. Originally I thought the game was made using the Source engine due to the familiarities in the graphics with the likes of Half Life 2 and Left 4 Dead, but the game is made using an engine called Diesel (made by GRIN, who are now defunct unfortunately). There are a couple of textures which are very low resolution which is a shame, but I can forgive this a bit given that a lot of the levels are actually fairly big, so this must have been done to reduce the need for loading screens.  The game has a really good ragdoll simulation too, when you are mowing down the enemies, they don’t just die in a normal fall to the floor fashion, each death is individually animated depending on where/how they were shot, which adds to the originality slightly. 

Payday is fully voice acted and done really well at that; the game is almost narrated by what seems to be someone behind the scenes instructing your team on what to do next on the heist. You’ll get remarks back from the rest of the team in responses to objectives being completed and you’ll also get a lot of radio chatter when you are in firefights with the police too. 

This is a really hard game. The first couple of heists come with the option to play them on easy mode; these must really be the games tutorial since they can be completed without any real problems; yet once you reach the third or fourth mission, the difficulty takes a big ramp up and you’ll actually find yourself either failing missions from not completing objectives, or because you have died or been taken into custody. I had to replay each of the last few stages of the game multiple times before I was able to successfully complete the heists. Even though the ramp in difficulty felt really harsh at the time; I began to enjoy the game even more because of it; because it’s not just as simple as a “get in and out” job, it forces you to plan your every move, and you will tread with caution around every corner because of the unknown ambush that awaits you. The game also has another two difficulty levels to be played on, Hard and overkill mode – these are modes which should not even be considered when playing on single player because you will not stand a chance. I tried the overkill mode out and it is just absolute carnage. I will definitely be asking friends to join in a game to give this mode a proper try out. 

Whilst all of the missions have the same key objective, and there is really only one way to complete said objective, it can lead to a little repetitive gameplay. The game does however try to counteract that by adding a little bit of randomness into the stages by shaking things up a bit; such as locations the locations of key civilians that you need to keep hostage, meaning you still have to go searching through the whole building to find them rather than rushing to the one place. Each of the levels has some form of random element to it which is nice to see, since you will be playing the same six or seven heists over and over again.

I have put about twenty hours into Payday: The Heist so far and see no end in sight for it at the moment. There is still a really active multiplayer scene if you want to just find pick up groups with randommers, but I would highly recommend playing this with a bunch of friends on Skype to get the full experience out of it. The added levels of difficulty also adds plenty of replay ability too; meaning you will not run out of interesting content for a long while with this title. The game does have one piece of DLC which includes new weapons and two new heists, which is a worthwhile piece of DLC. 

The game is also extremely technically sound too; I was able to play on 4k resolution with all of the graphic options maxed out and I was still able to hit the heights of 160 FPS, so this is one of the best optimized games out there at the moment.  Keyboard and mouse is recommended to play with, given the FPS nature.

Overall, Payday: The Heist is an extremely good game; one that I am surprised it has taken me so long to play, and one that I will certainly be keeping installed on my machine because of the high replay ability factor. The game is also very cheaply priced at £10,99 – but like I said at the start, the game is always going on sale, and most of the time it is for 90% off; at that price, is it an absolute no brainer to pick it up – you may as well pick up the four pack for yourself and friends whilst you are at it.

[h1]IN A WORD: [b]COMPELLING[/b] [/h1] 

[h1]IN SHORT:[/h1]
[quote=]
[b]WHAT TO EXPECT:[/b] Objective-based missions. Small number of heist maps. Dynamic events. Fun but difficult and intense gameplay.  Earn cash to level four specialist skill-trees.  Uunlock dozens of weapons and equipment.  Aging graphics. Hardest difficulties are extremely taxing.  Up to four player PvE coop. Patience needed to setup games on harder difficulties.  Solo play is not recommended.
[b]ACHIEVEMENTS:[/b] VERY DIFFICULT.  Most require COOP.
[b]STATUS:[/b] COMPLETE.
[b]WHEN TO BUY:[/b] BEFORE PAYDAY2. Rarely on sale.[/quote]

[i]More info below....[/i]

[h1]THE LOWDOWN:[/h1]
PAYDAY: The Heist is a hardcore COOP first-person shooter where players take on the role of a professional crew of heisters looking to undertake their next big score.  Guided by the off-screen A.I voiced coordinator called Bain, players must complete objectives before securing the loot and escaping.    Settings including: robbing a bank, stealing diamonds from an office to extracting toxic blood from a hospital ICU, amongst others. 

Gameplay occurs across alarmed, assault and sometimes stealth phases.  Security guards, thugs, mercenaries and every manner of law enforcement stand in the way of success.  A range of actions can be performed such as: reviving team-mates, exchanging hostages for captive players, shooting cameras, breaking through doors and using explosives (and more).  Players begin with basic weapons and equipment and level-up by completing objectives and missions.  The more cash stolen the faster they level, unlocking or upgrading weapons and equipment across four in-depth skill-trees.  Skill-based challenges give additional rewards for faster levelling.  

Random events keep players on their toes, forcing them to adapt their plans.  On the hardest difficulties the pace of the game is intense, where mistakes are punished, usually leading to a wipe. The game is stat heavy recording every action, every win or defeat, even accuracy.  A.I. bots take the place of crew members if not enough players are in-game.

[h1]THE GOOD:[/h1]
+ Great setting if you love anything about heist films like Heat.
+ Varied, detailed and robust heists, with detailed random events provides alot of replayability.
+ Requires highly skilled coop on harder difficulties.
+ Choose loadout from an extensive extensive range of assault weapons, sidearms, deployable munitions, specialist equipment and crew bonus modifier.
+ Reach level 193 across four specialist perks to unlock the full arsenal and equipment, and their upgrades.
+ Immersive soundtrack and voice-over interaction between characters.
+ Realistic enemy assault waves with the use of a combination of dynamic entry points, smoke grenades, snipers, tazers and shields and inflitrators to change-up player tactics.
+ Robust enemy A.I. behaviour  On the hardest level they are a real challenge for most players
+ DLC maps can be played by anyone as long as the host has the DLC.
+ All manner of enemy types to deal with including: security guards, thugs, police, various SWAT, FBI hostage extractors and specials; tazers, shields, cloakers and the tanky bulldozer.
+ Hundreds of skill-based challenges; x kills with weapon y, complete map z, collect $n... and much more!

[h1]THE BAD:[/h1]
- Could do with more than the nine (total) maps it has.
- Requires very good players to beat maps on harder difficulties.
- Learning the game mechanics on these harder levels is not a trivial exercise.
- Some achievements need a dedicated team of four players with good knowledge of the mechanics.
- A number of bugs exist with the interface and mechanics.
- During the day it can be a cheaters/hackers paradise.
- Game paused for players who join in-game.  Slows down play.
- Unstable netcode.  A fair amount of dropped connections.  Maybe 1/4 of games played.  Every one counts as a failed mission.  Either host or befriend players who are reliable hosts.
- Too many 'bad' players.  Some ragequit.  Especially bad if they are the host.
- Wolfpack DLC is required to level past level 145 and to obtain access to the technician skill-tree and associated weapons, munitions and equipment.
- No controller support.
- Game is now unsupported by the developers.

[h1]AND THE ORDINARY:[/h1]
* Graphics are good enough but, if you're into AAA titles they may seem dated.
* Needs more weapons only includes: four different handguns, five different primary and four secondary weapons.  Well-rendered though.  The use of a turret or tripwire mines is fun.
* The A.I. for friendly bots are flawed but can at least revive players on their own.

[h1]VERDICT:[/h1]
Payday: The Heist is one of those rare games that actually keeps you playing past the point that it should have.  Before you know it you will have wracked up hundreds of plays, perfected your strategies to a tee and spent 200+ hours obtaining all the challenges the game has to offer.  If only it were that simple!

The game is very good and captures alot of the qualities that made Heat such a great film with some excellent gameplay mechanics.  The combination of alternative objectives, law enforcement numbers and behaviour during assaults, the variety of random events, the range of weapons, deployable munitions and equipment makes each play a different experience from the last.  With the hundreds of skill-based challenges it all combines to give the game greater replayability despite the limited number of maps.

Knowing the maps, what weapons to bring and to use against which enemies is paramount to becoming a good player.  The biggest challenge for new players is to understand all the nuances of the mechanics, to learn the appropriate counters and timing of events and actions, especially firing from cover.  Otherwise they may not get the most out of this game.  Players start at the lowest difficulty and level the four skill-tree and only move on when they have the appropriate equipment and weapon unlocks.  Indeed the game is very challenging on the hardest difficulty.  Possibly the hardest of any coop PvE game I have played and therefore among the most fulfilling when everything clicks.  

Those aiming to complete the game's hardest difficulty will need to find a skilled group of players.  as completing them solo is virtually impossible.  At least for some maps. Lobbies almost always have a few cheaters/hackers who kill enemies without firing shot, or clear maps with one keystroke.  Getting hold of Dorentuz' excellent DorHud mod with its tools to weed out false players is vital.  Playing with inexperienced heisters can be just as maddening, especially if youre a stickler for stats.  Hosts can ragequit or giving you one less 'win' for that map.  You can get kicked by inexperienced players too.

If you can look past those faults there is a real gem of a game here.  It very rarely goes on sale, if ever and finding a good crew of skilled legtimate players can be hard at times.  Joining the Payday 5 Years group can help with this.  Though bear in mind only 100-200 players will be playing the game at any one time.  So organizing overkill and overkill+ games may take time to setup.  The facility for players to drop into games is archaic, sometimes pausing the game for a minute or two while their client syncs with the host.  If all of that doesnt put you off, then the aging graphics just may. 

Payday: The Heist is not an easy package to unwrap.  It does have great depth and requires brains and skilled finesse for the best experience.  Dont play the game like CoD or it will punish you.  If thats not enough to dissuade you or you want to try this before Payday 2, then its hard to point to another game that is as rewarding.  Just beware of  the lack of hand-holding.  Yet persistence wins the day.  Unfortunately I doubt you get this for a steal now.... as its only likley available at full-price.

[h2]I underestimated this game.[/h2]

Initially, I bought this game along with a DLC to get extra heists in Payday 2. After the purchase, the game sat in my library for about a year (or even longer), waiting for its moment. I can't say I was itching to play it; the graphics and clunky animations I'd seen in YouTube videos turned me off.

But as I was finishing up Payday 2, I decided to give this game a chance. I was incredibly surprised by how wrong I was about the project. The graphics look fine, the animations are good, and the gameplay is also interesting and different from the sequel. I got to know a still-active part of the game's community and it was quite interesting to compare it to Payday 2.

Most players stick with this game because it's harder, more interesting, or they simply prefer the OST more than in Payday 2. I personally fall somewhere in the middle. I enjoyed both games and had a great time playing them.

[b]I am also very grateful to [url=https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561198423580689]HunnckiSerfer[/url] for his help with the achievements (and to other players).[/b] If it weren't for him, I probably would have been working on them for a long time. Although many veteran players don't like that newcomers only join for achievements.

[b]To answer the question, "Is it worth playing?" it's up to your own discretion and desire. Each game in this series has its own pros and cons. But for me, my journey here ends.[/b]

Compared to Payday 2, this game is quite the challenge. No regenerating health, no converted cops, no godlike weapons.

You can't run in Rambo-style unless you're a masochist who enjoys dying every 30 seconds and getting put into custody constantly.

And hey, the Overdrill still exists if you really wanna have a "fun" challenge.

Once you start up Payday you can instantly see the resemblance to Heat, a Michael Mann-directed action movie. Every level is about a heist - you go in, you grab the money and you get out. In the meantime, dozens (if not hundreds) of cops are hurled against you. The 4 of you must work together to survive the level.

Every level has sections. You always have to do something before you can advance. For instance, you are in a hospital where your job is to steal blood samples. However, in order to proceed to the section of the special patients you need to cut through a door with a saw. These machines usually require activation. Still, you need to remain close by to see if they stop so that you can start them up again.The waves of enemies get more frequent and dangerous. Same goes for the bank mission: you cut through the safe, but oh wait, you need some thermite to be able to enter the vault.

Payday is one of those games where if you complete the levels you have pretty much seen everything. BUT! You have new weapons and other equipment to unlock once you level up. This so-called reputation level goes up till 193 and the higher level you are the more money you need to achieve the next level.

Essentially, the replayability goes along the road Killing Floor has. Higher levels make you stronger (due to the new equipment) so you are able to pick a higher difficulty and replay the heists once more. Or die trying as this game is VERY difficult. Even on normal difficulty you will sweat to see the end of the road. And then you have at least 200 achievements waiting to be unlocked. :)

PAYDAY is a fun game. If you have a lot of time on your hands and you like "farming" this is for you.

Imagine Left 4 Dead except you're shooting cops instead of zombies.

There's a level progression system in the game just like in the sequel, but you don't have to worry about any of the RPG bullshit elements, just level up and spend points. Imagine more like Killing Floor where playing the game gives you progress  on each class. You can grind it out to get there faster, but that'll go against what the game's pushing you towards.

People say it's comparable to Payday 2 in that they're the same characters and world, etc. They're wrong. The game is paced completely differently: heists aren't meant to be quick in-and-out situations, they're long, gruelling marathons you have to push through. They also don't function on an "all or nothing" reward system. If you fail right at the end, that's okay, you still get money (experience) for every objective you completed along the way. It's not as rage inducing as fucking up a Big Bank stealth right as you're opening the vault, then having to run and get the god damn drill because alarms went off.

That's another thing, there's not really stealth save for one or two missions. Don't be a fuckin' bitch ass pussy. When you ask yourself "Are we rushin' in, or are we goin in sneakypeaky like?", the answer should always be the former. Stealth in this game is a lot harder, and it's more of a dickwaving contest kind of situation when you can stealth the few maps, rather than being the optimal strategy necessarily.

Overall, it's worth picking up even if you have Payday 2. It's not like the Left 4 Dead series in the regards that L4D2 replaces the 1st in every way, they're just completely different games with different mechanics.

After putting nearly 240 hours on this game, I can definitely say that this is THE definitive heisting experience. The thing about Payday 2 is that it started off playing very similarly to this game. But as more updates and DLC were added, the second game slowly became a shadow of its former self. Obviously everyone knows this game is harder, but something I really like about this game over the second that I don't feel many people admire as much as they should have is how the gang actually reacts to the situation they're in, which helps a lot with immersion. The cops feel incredibly alive as well, it feels like you're fighting against an actual police force and not just a horde of zombies dressed up as cops you see in the second game. The cops in this game are much more tactical and insanely fun to fight, and the voice lines they say in this game work the same as in the first FEAR, you have to listen to them in order to know what they'll pull off. This game handles leveling way better too when compared to the other games. In Payday 2, money quickly becomes meaningless after you play like 10 heists. But in this game, money IS the main way to level up. This means that money will always be important no matter what, so there is always some incentive to take everything and leave nothing behind.

Enemy variety is great in this game too. Of course, you have your special enemies like bulldozers and cloakers, but I'm mostly referring to your common enemies. In the beginning of a heist, when things go loud, first responders arrive at the scene. These first responders are your normal, everyday cops that are equipped with either pistols or shotguns. But as the heist goes on, they slowly get replaced with heavy SWAT units. Something I love in this game is that you will still see regular cops helping SWAT in the early to mid game, which really does help with enemy variety. In the other 2 payday games, those regular cops disappear after the first assault wave, if not, by the second. Also, during assault breaks where there's not much going on, you'll have to deal with FBI units that come in small teams. They're incredibly weak, and they mostly specialize in going after any hostages you take, or freeing any civilians that happen to still be around the area.

I got to say, I really do prefer this game over the sequel, and this is coming from someone who has played many more hours on the second game compared to the first. It's just unfortunate that there's not many people playing this masterpiece anymore since Payday 2 easily overshadows this game. The second game is fun, but there are definitely reasons to come back to this game for a more grounded and serious tone that puts an emphasis on teamwork to make succeed

Comparing this game to PAYDAY 2, I generally prefer PAYDAY: The Heist for the following points:

1. The "loud" is more fun here than in PD2.
2. "Diamond Heist" doesn't have any client lag during stealth.
3. The DLC is worth the price compared to many other PD2 DLCs.
4. Masks are better and more in focus than in PD2.
5. It more likely focuses you to play with other people, than solo.
    - The heists are tough on highest difficulty, most of them impossible to be done with 2 standard players, sometimes even 3 standard players.
6. Bain interacts more with the crew than he does in PD2.
7. 2h Overdrill on Overkill 145+
8. The Overkill 145+ difficulty.
9. Overkill 145+ in general is more difficult than Death Wish (except you play PD2, PD:TH style)
10. Undercover special waves...

I prefer playing PD2 for the following reasons:

1. Way more heists.
2. You can easily solo run most of the heists (due to stealth).
3. Stealth may be more interesting if you build the correct "challenges".
4. You have more options what you could do in PD2, than in PD:TH.

General ups (+) and downs (-) (most of them already mentioned):

+ Way more co-op based
+ It's harder (on the highest difficulty, default)
+ Love those masks...
+ Very nice soundtracks
+ Focus on co-op
- No Mercy has certain stealth issues
- There's no focus on stealth in PD:TH, it's in general about "loud"
- Singlplayer works on Hard difficulty but is a pain on higher difficulties
- Lots of hackers who can ruin your gaming experience.

There's probably even many more points, which I probably forgot to mention. :)

Payday: The Heist** is a cooperative first-person shooter that puts players in the shoes of professional criminals pulling off a variety of high-stakes heists. Developed by Overkill Software, it offers fast-paced, intense gameplay with a focus on teamwork and strategy. Here’s a short breakdown of its key aspects:

**Gameplay**
--------------------
- **Heist Missions:** The game revolves around six unique heists, ranging from bank robberies to prison breakouts. Each mission feels distinct, with objectives that can change based on how the players perform.
- **Co-op Multiplayer:** Payday is best enjoyed with friends, as teamwork is essential for managing hostages, cracking safes, and fighting off waves of police forces. Solo players are supported by AI teammates, but they lack the strategic depth and coordination of human partners.
- **Dynamic Events:** No heist plays out exactly the same way twice. The game features random events like security camera placements, police attack points, and the behavior of NPCs, adding a layer of unpredictability.
- **Combat and Shooting Mechanics:** The gunplay is solid, though not as polished as more modern shooters. However, the variety of weapons and gadgets keeps the combat engaging.
- **Progression:** Players earn money and experience points to unlock better weapons, equipment, and skills, adding a satisfying progression loop to the game.

 **Pros:**
------------
- Intense and engaging heist scenarios.
- Strong emphasis on teamwork and coordination.
- Dynamic mission structure keeps gameplay fresh.
  
 **Cons:**
----------------
- AI teammates can feel lackluster compared to playing with real players.
- Limited mission variety (only six heists at launch).

[h2]**Verdict:**[/h2]
---------------------------
 *Payday: The Heist* is a fun, adrenaline-pumping game that shines when played with a group. While it has some dated mechanics and limited mission selection, its cooperative design and dynamic scenarios make it a thrilling experience for fans of team-based shooters.

Payday: The Heist is fifteen years old this year, and it's still possibly one of the greatest horde shooters of all time. That includes some fierce modern competition: Helldivers, Killing Floor, and even its own sequels. None can quite beat the first Payday.

The gunplay is smooth and the heists are perfect. Every weapon handles well (they better, since there are so few), and the four upgrade trees provide clear goals and make every weapon (and its upgrades) feel like a reward. Cops die when you hit them in the head and are not bullet sponges, but neither are you: You are incredibly vulnerable, especially at higher levels, and one mistake or tactical error can cost you an entire heist (and wonderfully, make it feel like your fault, not the game's). You die in seconds, but so do the enemies. At higher difficulties, it almost becomes a strategy game. The gameplay loop is without error: Assault, cooldown, and assault again, and between these things try to do an objective, but the originality and flair of each heist never makes it boring.

It eats the lunch of the movie Heat: Every heist has a punctual story, growing in volume until it comes to a bombastic finish (usually involving a large explosion or a helicopter). The characters are obnoxious, but not annoying. Apart from personal taste, it's almost impossible to hate any single character. Bain is a perfect announcer, and all four heisters are every movie archetype (The cool leader, the aggressive-but-cautious brawler, the suave cockney bruiser, and the downright insane pyromaniac). Their voice acting is personable and their personalities are worked into the heist through dialogue and conversations, making the game feel more like an interactive movie than a mindless shoot-em-up.

The story seems unimportant, but in combination with all other things perfects the game. No Payday game has actually managed to reach the heights of Payday 1's story. It is beautifully simple: It is the movie Heat, Point Break, and the bank heist scene from The Dark Knight, with all of the aesthetics and flair and none of the fat of a complicated story. The small selection of heists and the complexity of each creates a linear 'crime spree', with each heist growing more bombastic and ludicrous over time.

This all combines to create an experience that is completely unique. No other game, even its sequels, is like it. It does not feel like you are playing a game, but living out your own heist movie. It is creative, it is funny, it is simple, and it never gets boring. Get this game if you know what's good for you.

‘Payday: The Heist” is a fast-paced, edgy, co-operative first-person shooter (FPS) that takes its inspiration in no small part from the fantastic Michael Mann heist flick ‘Heat’. A pulsating background score, tense entry and setup sequences, interspersed with absolute chaos once the heist is underway, make this probably one of the best Heist games ever made.

[b][u]Campaign | Gameplay:[/u][/b] Released by Overkill Software / Sony Entertainment in 2011, the game consists of 7 Heists that can be played in Single-player or Co-op mode, with an additional 2 Heists available as DLC. Gamers choose to play as one of the four main protagonists – Dallas, Hoxton, Wolf or Chains – each a specialist in his own area of Heavy Weapons, Explosives, Engineering/Tech, and Sniper/Support. Each heist also consists of a series of sub-objectives – which may include locating a key target (such as a bank manager), gaining access to restricted locations, destroying surveillance footage etc. Additionally, the fact that components of these sub-objectives will randomly spawn in various locations on the map ensures that no two playthrough’s of a particular heist are exactly alike - a major bonus to the overall replayability of this title. While playable in Single-player mode (supported by 3 AI controlled bots), the game absolutely shines in Multiplayer / Co-op where each member of your 4-man crew is a different player. Obviously, the quality of your experience and ultimate success of the heist will depend on the experience of your crew – but being part of a well drilled team provides an adrenaline rush that few other games will match.

[b][u]Flaws:[/u][/b] In considering its shortcomings (and there are a few) – Lack of a single player campaign, short overall length (limited to 7 Heists), average graphics, somewhat clunky K&M controls (/no controller support), text-based UI, and an overall experience targeted at a narrow cross-section of the gaming community, you might think this is a game to pass on. But,… what it does, it does brilliantly well – and the thrill of running through a heist with a top-notch crew who work together, seamlessly combine to complete objectives, cover each other’s backs and take scores is something well worth the experience. 

‘Payday: The Heist’ ultimately succeeds as an homage to the great heist flicks of the past – it’s slick, fast-paced, offers a good variety of heists, and is supported by a phenomenal soundtrack. Robert de Niro (in ‘Heat’) tells it like it is: “We do what we do best – Take Scores. You do what you do best – Try to stop guys like us”. Strongly Recommended for Online Co-op / with Friends! – Rated (7.9/10)

It is my honest belief that Payday: The Heist is THE Payday game. It still holds up all these years later and often outperforms its successors even. Oh, and by the way the screenshots on the store page are inaccurate to the actual game for some reason, so don't worry. The game doesn't look that out of date. I suppose that's a fitting transition.

Visuals 
Payday: The Heist's graphics are visually dated, but they're not bad. They're still able to convey what you need to know and it all fits the overall artstyle. Payday: The Heist went for a more gritty and industrial theme similar to early Payday 2, and it overall adds a lot of atmosphere to the game. All the cop designs look good, are visually distinct while still remaining consistent.

The Soundtrack 
It wouldn't be a Payday review without mentioning it. Speaking of Payday, of course they're all amazing. All of them fit the game perfectly with their more industrial undertones, and even the party music that plays during Diamond heist as an easter egg are amazing. They're all great and more than good enough to listen to outside of the game. Simon Viklund's work is timeless.

Characters 
Unlike Payday 2 or 3 the characters in this game will speak to eachother over the course of a heist. They'll comment on things that occur during a heist, tell eachother things to do (such as to grab the thermite on First World Bank), and sound more nervous and intense in their voicelines during an assault compared to when they're not. Small things like this adds a lot of life to the characters and improves the atmosphere of the game. This is a feature I was hoping to see in Payday 3 and I was disappointed when it was absent. In Payday 2 or 3 you'll generally only hear your heisters speak either when they kill a special, they're hurt, or answering a pager in stealth. They don't feel alive and it's what made the saying "Payday characters are defined by their gloves and their accents".

Availability
The game instantly one-ups Payday 3 by running on peer-to-peer matchmaking. It also has a server browser for multiplayer, something that at the time of writing Payday 3 lacks.
The game can be bought for very cheap on sale and it only has one DLC, unlike its sequel. That one DLC is also the hands down best DLC this series ever got, so it's definitely worth picking up alongside the game. The game runs a lot easier than 2 and it takes up less than 7 gigs, in comparison to the sequel that takes 86 due to all the content added over the years.

Gameplay
In terms of gameplay this game is a lot slower paced than the two games that came after it. The game rewards a more methodical play style and teamwork is more essential on higher difficulties than in Payday 2. For a soon to be 12 year old game that was made by an indie team this game is really balanced. There are a few weapon balance issues, but in terms of the cops and players the difficulties are incredibly balanced. Even the hardest difficulty is fair despite it being very punishing. Unlike Payday 2 where you can get sniped by a heavy swat that made up roughly 10 pixels on your screen and you die before you can react, in Payday: The Heist the cops are tough but fair.

Assault breaks in this game are much better. Since cover is much more important with less ways to stun cops, you'll often find yourself running out of ammo more during assaults, though you get a chance to replenish ammo easier during the assault break. Assault breaks also last significantly longer which gives you a chance to get back on your feet, recover from an assault and trade teammates from custody. The assault breaks are more realistic. In Payday 2 the assault breaks are so short that you can literally have assaults start 10 seconds after the previous one ended. At that point they may aswell not end at all.

Weapons
Payday: The Heist has 13 guns (5 primaries, 4 secondaries, 4 handguns), which doesn't sound like a lot in comparison to Payday 2, but the difference being the weapons themselves. Because the weapons are much fewer they're able to be more varied, and not one gun does the exact same thing as another. Sure, there are some balance issues as I briefly mentioned, some weapons are better than others, but apart from maybe the starter pistol they're all completely viable for the high difficulties.

This and the limited number of heists, is what I assume turns some people off from this game, since all the content is already in the sequel. However, what the game lacks in variety, it makes up for in quality. Despite only having 9 heists they're all great and replayable. I always believed that the Classics were the best heists in Payday 2, and since those nine are what this game consists of, well you get it. The game is varied enough to not get stale too quickly, but is limited enough to where there's not any bloat or weapons that are essentially re-skins of one another.

Conclusion:
Payday: The Heist is a great game. It did everything Payday 3 tried to but better, and for only a few bucks when on sale. This was the first game I got 100% achievements in. I didn't do it because I had to, I didn't even plan to. In fact the only reason I played the game originally was to go back to the roots of Payday to see how it holds up, and I was shocked at how well it not only holds up, but also does better than the sequel. I 100%ed it because it was fun, and it still is. There's a reason the game is the highest rated game out of the Payday franchise. To call back to the beginning of the review: If there's any of the three games I recommend you buy, it is this one. Payday: The Heist is worth your time and money.

What is Payday The Heist?

Well, it's a 4 player coop game. In short, you play as heisters and the whole game is basically centered against defending yourself against incoming waves of enemies.

The objective is usually to steal something, but there are obstacles inbetween. Drills are the most common equipment used to break through them, and they are fully passive. All you have to do is plant it, and wait till the timer runs out. If the drill jams, you unjam it.

Then there is the escape, which usually requires you to go back the way you came from.

The levels get more complicated. There is one that requires you to defend a power fuse. In that level, power is required to run a server that is used to decrypt some files. Getting the power turned off basically stops the "timer". The server and the power fuse are in different locations, so usually one or two are required to stay back and guard it.

[h1]Levels[/h1]

The original game consists of 6 levels.

Unlike Payday 2 or The Wolf's DLC, the original heists don't offer much variety. You can't really go full stealth for example. There is one level that has stealth, but it's partial. 

Overkill also added an extra level called No Mercy. It's free and is inspired by Left 4 Dead, and even sort of acts as a unofficial prologue to the events of Left 4 Dead.

No Mercy & The Wolf DLC are basically the foundation of Payday 2. They are centered around dynamic events. Every time you play them, they may have items appearing at different locations, and random events happening at times.

[h1]In depth look on mechanics[/h1]

The game has 3 special enemies: Bulldozer, Taser and Cloaker. It also have cops with shields and standard cops (their armor depends on the difficulty level). I think it's a very important aspect of the game. It keeps the gameplay from getting dull throughout the level.

The game has armor and health: armor outlines your characters avatar in bottom right, and it can regenerate, health on the other hand can't. When you get 0 health you will be put into bleedout (last stand), after that you can either be put into custody or get saved by your teammates. Your teammates can also trade you for a hostage if you get into custody.

The game also has a leveling system. 145 levels, though it's 193 if you get the DLC. You get 3 unlock trees (4 with DLC).  Each tree has 48 unlocks, and that's how you get new items, weapons and so on. 

It was kind of hard figuring out how to switch from one tree to another. You need to hold Tab, and either press [1], [2], [3] or [4]. By the end of the level, points are added to that tree. 

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]

The game also has great atmosphere i would say, and the coop mechanics are on par with Left 4 Dead. The game has a lot of difficulty levels, so the game never really feels too easy. It feels hard enough to require the cooperation of all teammates, which i feel is really important. There were plenty of memorable moments i really from this game.

Friendly fire is off though (thankfully), so backstabbing is not a thing.

Personally i really like Payday's coop mechanics. Payday 1 is miles behind Payday 2, but the coop mechanics are pretty much the same in both games, and that what kept me playing for this long.

[h1]DLC Compromise[/h1]

The game also has one DLC - The Wolf. It features 2 levels, but it's not necessary for you to buy the DLC to play the levels. You can join anyone who owns the DLC and play it for free. That's not a bug by the way, it's actually a really nice policy that guys at Overkill support. If you want the guns and the new upgrade tree, you will have to purchase the DLC though. It's a really fair compromise in my opinion, and most importantly, it doesn't split the community.
